title: Halcyon Pet Foods — Valuation Analysis: Entry Investment Committee Materials — September 2017
summary: Comps analysis and entry valuation workbook prepared by Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II deal team for the Halcyon Pet Foods entry IC in September 2017. The workbook includes a public comparable companies set (premium pet pure-plays: Blue Buffalo, Freshpet; diversified pet/consumer: Central Garden & Pet, Spectrum Brands, J.M. Smucker, TreeHouse Foods), a precedent M&A transaction set covering premium pet food deals from 2010–2017, and a valuation sensitivity table. LTM Adjusted EBITDA per EY QofE is $25.9M. The selected entry multiple is 11.0x, implying an enterprise value of approximately $285M. Public comps trade at 11.5–16.0x NTM EBITDA and 13.0–18.5x LTM EBITDA; the selected entry multiple represents a ~30% discount to public comps and ~20% discount to recent strategic transactions. The upside exit case assumes 14.0x.

growth_drivers: Premium pet food market expansion
Public comparables scarcity value for premium-pet pure-plays
Strategic acquirer appetite for premium pet platforms
risks: Smaller scale supports lower-to-mid end of valuation range at entry
30% discount to public comps required to establish margin of safety
Multiple expansion to exit 14.0x dependent on sustained strategic interest

title: Halcyon Pet Foods — Final Returns Summary
summary: Final returns summary for Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II's investment in Halcyon Pet Foods, a premium pet food platform acquired in September 2017 and exited via strategic sale to Cabrillo Holdings (Mars-affiliated) in April 2023. The deal produced a 3.5x gross MOIC and 28.4% gross IRR over a 5.6-year hold, representing the highest gross MOIC in Fund II. Value creation was driven by organic revenue growth, margin/mix improvement, multiple expansion (11.0x → 14.5x), and one bolt-on acquisition (Vesta Treats, Jun 2020). DTC channel revenue grew from 14.6% to 42.1% of total revenue. Realized outcomes fell between base and upside underwrite cases on most metrics, with DTC penetration and exit multiple exceeding the base case.

growth_drivers: Organic revenue growth (CAGR ~16% from FY17 to FY22)
DTC channel build from 14.6% to 42.1% of revenue
Multiple expansion from 11.0x to 14.5x
Vesta Treats bolt-on acquisition (Jun 2020, $18M EV)
Premiumization evidenced by rising average unit retail price (FY17=100 → FY23=135)
risks: Extended hold of 5.6 years vs. 5-year underwrite
Margin expansion tempered by elevated digital marketing investment
Residual customer concentration in PetSmart/Petco (31% at exit, down from 59% at entry)

title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation: Halcyon Pet Foods, Inc.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II entry IC memo recommending approval of the acquisition of Halcyon Pet Foods, Inc. (Boulder, CO), a premium/natural pet food maker, at an enterprise value of $285M (11.0x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $25.9M). Atlas Crossing commits $95M of equity alongside a $190M Antares Capital unitranche, with founder Dr. Marcus Reyes rolling over 12% of proceeds. The investment thesis centers on the premium pet food category's structural tailwinds (~9% CAGR), an underdeveloped DTC channel (14.6% → 35%+ target), gross margin expansion (~530bps), management gap-filling (CFO, COO, Head of DTC hires), and a bolt-on M&A path in adjacent premium categories. Base case projects a 5-year hold delivering 2.6x gross MOIC and ~22% gross IRR on a $648M exit EV at 12.0x. Key risks include customer concentration (PetSmart + Petco = 59% of revenue), founder dependency, private label encroachment, and commodity input volatility. IC approval is recommended subject to confirmatory diligence, final debt papers, and founder rollover documentation.

key_quotes.quote: Underdeveloped DTC channel = clear margin and growth lever. DTC represented only 14.6% of FY2016 revenue; comparable premium-pet brands (Ollie, Blue Buffalo, Stella & Chewy's) operate at 25–40% DTC. Migration from specialty retail to DTC should drive ~530bps of GM expansion over the hold period plus accelerated organic growth.

Authentic brand built around a defensible founder story. Founded by a practicing veterinarian (Dr. Marcus Reyes, DVM) who reformulated dog food after his own dog's GI issues. Brand resonates with conscious pet parents and commands a $1.20–$1.40 per-pound premium vs. private label. Net Promoter Score of 76 (best-in-class for the category).

Top 2 customers (PetSmart, Petco) represent 59% of FY2017E revenue — material concentration. Offset: 7-year supply agreement with PetSmart and 5-year with Petco, both with auto-renewals. DTC channel build over the hold period reduces concentration to ~30% by year 5.

Founder/CEO has built a $130M-revenue business with limited outside capital but has not built a CFO function, integrated DTC tech stack, or scale supply chain. Our playbook (CFO upgrade, IT investments, supply-chain advisory) maps directly to the gaps.
Base-case projections indicate a 5-year hold delivering 2.6x gross MOIC and a ~22% gross IRR; upside case (full DTC plan execution + one bolt-on + multiple expansion) supports 3.6x and ~29%.

growth_drivers: Premium/natural pet food category growing at ~9% CAGR driven by humanization and millennial pet ownership
DTC channel underdeveloped at 14.6% of revenue vs. 25–40% for comparable brands — significant margin and growth lever
Gross margin expansion of ~530bps targeted via DTC mix shift, packaging redesign, and co-packer renegotiation
Management capability upgrades: CFO, COO, and Head of DTC hires
Bolt-on M&A in adjacent premium categories (treats, freeze-dried toppers)
Multiple expansion plausible given recent strategic exits at 13–17x EBITDA
risks: Customer concentration: PetSmart + Petco = 59% of FY2017E revenue
Founder dependency on Dr. Marcus Reyes (CEO/brand figurehead)
Private label encroachment in mass and specialty retail channels
E-commerce competitive intensity from VC-funded DTC entrants (Ollie, The Farmer's Dog)
Multiple compression risk at exit given elevated category sentiment

title: Exit Recommendation — Halcyon Pet Foods, Inc. | Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II IC Memorandum
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II exit IC memo recommending sale of Halcyon Pet Foods, Inc. to Cabrillo Holdings (Mars-affiliated) for $890M enterprise value (14.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $61.4M). The all-cash stock purchase transaction is targeting an April 14, 2023 close. Fund II invested $104M in equity (initial $95M in Sep 2017 + $9M bolt-on for Vesta Treats in Jun 2020) and expects cumulative proceeds of $355M (including $21M Q3 2021 dividend recap), yielding 3.5x gross MOIC and 28.4% gross IRR on a ~5.5-year hold. Net MOIC is 2.8x and net IRR is 23.1%. Key value creation drivers include DTC channel build (subscriber count grew 6.5x), organic revenue growth (51% of equity value creation), multiple expansion from 11.0x to 14.5x (29%), and the Vesta Treats bolt-on (8%). Revenue grew from $132M to $328M and EBITDA from $25.9M to $61.4M over the hold period. The memo notes three competing final bids and recommends Cabrillo for highest bid, all-cash structure, and strategic synergies with Mars global distribution.

key_quotes.quote: Returns: 3.5x gross MOIC and ~28% gross IRR to Atlas Crossing Fund II — a top-quartile outcome and the highest MOIC delivered by the fund to date.

DTC build was the single largest value driver. Hired Head of DTC in Q1 2018; rebuilt tech stack 2018–2019 (CDP, marketing automation, owned subscription engine). Subscriber count grew 6.5× over the hold period.

Premium-pet category multiples are currently elevated (clean assets pricing 14–17x) but show early signs of moderation as inflation persists and discretionary consumer spend faces pressure... Further hold increases the risk of negative multiple drift outweighing incremental EBITDA growth.

Plan was $4–6M over 18 months; actual investment was $11M over 24 months. Should have approved the larger envelope at close. Lesson: for DTC-heavy plans, double the IT-investment budget at underwriting and treat ahead-of-curve infra as defensive.

Held to a single co-packer for wet food until Q4 2021; freight pressure 2021–2022 caused service-level dips. Should have moved to dual-source wet by mid-2020. Cost in lost revenue (quantified internally at ~$8M).

growth_drivers: DTC channel build — subscriber count grew 6.5x over hold period
Organic revenue growth 2.5x from $132M to $328M
Vesta Treats bolt-on acquisition (Jun 2020) driving cross-sell
Premium pet category tailwind — 11% CAGR realized through 2022
Gross margin expansion of +490bps over hold period
Pricing discipline — AUR +35% vs. CPI +21%
risks: EBITDA margin compression of 85bps due to digital marketing investment and supply-chain inflation
Manufacturing footprint reliance on single co-packer for wet food until Q4 2021
Pricing actions considered too conservative through inflation cycle
Multiple moderation risk in premium-pet category as discretionary spend faces pressure
